audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on five of seven rows. Full reads Annie/Annie/Annie/Skill/Annie/Kassadin/Kassadin; content win[] reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie. Content also contradicts itself: win[6] says Annie while whys[6] says 2+ items favours Kassadin.
audit.why: Annie is 48.31% over 563 games — she does not own the lane outright. Levels 1-3 are genuinely even (no blink for him, no reach for her), 4-6 through first item are Annie's window because Riftwalk is unaffordable, and 2+ items is Kassadin's because Riftwalk reaches a 2s cooldown at rank 3 and Void Stone reduces the magic damage that is Annie's entire kit.
audit.corrected: Chart becomes Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie/Kassadin. Full flips rows 0-3 and 5; content flips win[6] to Kassadin. Ratings 5/5/5/6/7/6/3.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why described a late game Annie flips with one button, which is the opposite of the recorded side and of whys[6].
audit.why: Riftwalk at rank 3 is a 2-second, 500-range blink; Tibbers is a 600-range zone he simply leaves. Void Stone's magic damage reduction compounds it.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why now states the 2s Riftwalk and Void Stone as the reason the row is his.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real interactions were absent: Void Stone reduces magic damage (Annie deals nothing else), Null Sphere leaves him a shield that specifically absorbs magic damage, and Force Pulse charges from spells cast in his vicinity — including Annie's own stacking spells.
audit.why: Riot's text states all three. The passive plus the Q shield is why an Annie combo that kills other mids leaves Kassadin alive, and it is why Void Staff is a real purchase here rather than a luxury.
audit.corrected: Added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, enemyWin, phases[0].why and report[8].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flags zero sequencing advice; breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3, so his escape gets strictly better with levels — the kill window is at 6, not later. Force Pulse is 21s down to 17s and needs charging.
sources: enemyKit R and E cooldown fields

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flags wants.foe[1] "Use Nether Blade" as a probable wrong name. It is a false positive — Nether Blade is Kassadin's real W in the kit file. Left untouched.

edits.before: Q last-hits refund mana on kill — farm with it for free and let the stun counter tick where he can see it.
edits.after: Q last-hits refund mana — farm free and stack, but Void Stone means every point of your damage lands reduced.

edits.before: Hold the four-stack glow and watch him orbit at max range — a stocked Annie controls the lane by standing there.
edits.after: Hold the four-stack glow — he has no escape until 6, so a stun inside 625 is a free chunk or a kill with a gank.

edits.before: Late Annie flips fights with one button: flash-Tibbers the clump, peel with the bear, and re-stock off the chaos.
edits.after: Riftwalk hits a 2s cooldown at rank 3 and Void Stone cuts your magic damage — he blinks out of Tibbers at will now.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Molten Shield for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 falling to 2s at rank 3, so the escape window closes as he levels it — kill him at 6, not at 11. - Force Pulse charges off spells cast near him, including yours; stack on the wave, not in his face.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to 11: Void Stone eats your magic damage and 2-second Riftwalks make Tibbers a target he leaves.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry by ending it early — every minute you spend farming even is a minute Void Stone and Riftwalk are worth more.

edits.before: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk he answered with nothing.
edits.after: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk out re-stacking — pre-6 he has no blink, so the only answer is his Q shield.

edits.before: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk he answered with nothing.
edits.after: Null Sphere leaves him a shield that absorbs magic damage — bait it onto your Molten Shield, then stun into a naked Kassadin.

edits.before: Kassadin spends Riftwalk early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Tibbers burns anyone standing near him — a Riftwalk onto you lands him inside the aura.

edits.before: That’s Kassadin’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: An unstacked Annie with a shoved wave is exactly the picture Riftwalk is looking for.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Luden's or Stormsurge into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs dive — cast it mid-Tibbers.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Luden's into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame — Void Stone's magic reduction makes Void Staff a real buy before Rabadon's.

notes: DERIVED FLAG MISFIRE: enemyKit lists Kassadin's Null Sphere with flag "channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it", and missingInteractions carries a channel-interruptible rule saying Pyromania/Tibbers cancels it. Riot's own description says the opposite — Null Sphere is what INTERRUPTS channels; it is not itself a channel. Trusted the description and did NOT write that interaction anywhere. Recommend the rule be suppressed for kassadin so other agents do not ship it. packet.suspectNames flagged "Use Nether Blade" as a wrong name; it is correct (his real W) and was left alone.
